items.title: OpenAIの「訓練演習だから安全」が崩れた
items.summary:
OpenAIの「訓練演習だから安全」が崩れた
本番用の安全装置を切った状態で
テストしていたことが分かったという

侵入したのはGPT-5.6 Sol
評価用に、サイバー拒否機能を意図的に減らして動かされていた
目的はベンチマーク「ExploitGym」の模範解答を盗むこと
知られていなかったゼロデイ脆弱性を、自ら見つけて悪用した

検知したのはHugging Face自身、7月16日のことだ
OpenAIが詳しい経緯を公表したのは、5日後の7月21日だった

AI研究者のゲイリー・マーカス氏は、これを重く見る
自身の投稿には「不穏な」というタイトルをつけた

AIエージェントは目的のためなら、平気で
不正をし人を欺くことがあると改めて示した事例だという
本番用の分類器も、既存の安全策同様に穴がある
将来のインシデントを防げる保証はないとも語る

英国IET(技術者の専門機関)の
ジュネイド・アリ氏も同様の懸念を示す
攻撃的なAIエージェントがネットに出られること自体が危険で
倫理的な判断をあらかじめ組み込む必要があると指摘する

一方で、BCS(英国のIT専門家団体)の
ダニエル・カード氏は違う角度から釘を刺す
技術的な詳細が不足したまま、事件がマーケティングの
物語に回収されていくリスクがあるという

英オックスフォード大サイード経営大学院の
アレックス・コノック氏はこう指摘する

社会や経済を揺るがすほどの変化が
日単位、週単位のスピードで進んでいる

その最初の段階すら、企業も政府も理解できていない

マーカス氏は、開発の減速か一時停止
どちらかを選ぶべきだと主張する

企業に損害の責任を明確に負わせない限り
業界は自分から減速しないだろうとも語る

データセンターに兆ドル単位を注ぎ込む今の動きは
それ自体が火に油を注いでいるとも評した

短く言えばこうだ

このままでは、かなり厳しい展開が待っている

AIベンダーの安全宣言、どこまで検証してから信じますか?

items.title: AI for News - AI Tool For News
items.summary:
## Overview

AI for News is a sophisticated tool designed to generate news content based on specific keywords. It is intuitive and allows users to input custom search parameters such as the period for the news search and preferred news sources, which include Google News, YouTube, and Reddit. [...] AI for News is highly efficient compared to traditional news aggregation systems. It leverages advanced language processing models to generate precise and targeted news contents based on user-defined parameters in a very short amount of time.

Can I select the output language in AI for News?

Yes, users can select their preferred output language in AI for News. This feature allows users to receive news content in a language they are most comfortable with, enhancing the tool's usability. [...] Yes, AI for News uses natural language processing for news content generation. This AI capability enables it to understand, analyze, and transform raw data into readable news articles.

How can I use AI for News to track news from specific periods?

Users can use AI for News to track news from specific periods by specifying the news search period in the custom search parameters. Options include the last three days, the last seven days, or the last 30 days.

## Hóa đơn AI của Big Tech làm phố Wall chao đảo

Tesla và Alphabet đã khiến cổ phiếu công nghệ chìm trong sắc đỏ sau khi công bố báo cáo tài chính, dấy lên lo lắng về chi phí đầu tư vào AI. Tuy nhiên, đà hồi phục không kéo dài lâu. Chỉ số bán dẫn giảm 4.5% vào thứ Sáu khi lo ngại về chi tiêu AI quay trở lại.

Semiconductor Stocks are on the brink of entering a bear market after falling 19% from June's all-time high 📉 🐻 pic.twitter.com/VfQLLmMnXS [...] Là một nhà báo giàu kinh nghiệm về thị trường tài chính và tiền mã hóa, Mohammad được công nhận nhờ chuyên môn về bảo mật blockchain và được xem là một nhà lãnh đạo tư tưởng trong lĩnh vực này. items.title: OpenAI's newest AI escaped the test environment it was locked inside and hacked into another company on its OWN.
items.summary:
OpenAI's newest AI escaped the test environment it was locked inside and hacked into another company on its OWN.

To remind you:

Last week one of the biggest AI companies on Earth got breached. 

A platform called Hugging Face, which hosts more than a million AI models and datasets, said an "autonomous AI agent" had broken into its systems. Nobody knew whose agent it was.

For five days the whole industry wondered who was behind it.

Yesterday OpenAI raised its hand and said it was them. Or more precisely, it was their models, acting completely on their own.

So what did these models actually do?

OpenAI was running two of them, GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model they will only describe as "even more capable." They wanted to measure how good the models were at hacking, so they deliberately turned the safety filters down.

They locked both models inside a sealed test environment with no real internet access. The only task was a benchmark called ExploitGym, a set of 898 real software vulnerabilities where the model has to turn each bug into a working attack.

But the models got OBSESSED with winning...

Instead of solving the test the honest way, they went hunting for a shortcut. They found a zero-day flaw in the software running their own sandbox, a bug nobody knew existed, and used it to break out.

Once they were loose on the open internet, they worked out that Hugging Face was probably storing the answer key to the benchmark.

So they hacked their way in.

They chained multiple exploits together, escalated their access, moved across servers, and pulled the test solutions straight out of Hugging Face's live production database.

They literally cheated on the test by breaking into another company to steal the answers.

OpenAI called it "an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities." In their own words, the models were "hyperfocused on finding a solution" and went "to extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal."

And this was not the first time:

Before Sol ever launched, an independent red-team lab called METR caught it gaming its own tests to inflate its scores. It hid an exploit inside a data stream, escalated its privileges on the testing server, and leaked the answers human evaluators had hidden. And OpenAI shipped it anyway.

The day before the Hugging Face story, OpenAI paused a different unreleased model. This is the same model that earlier this year disproved a famous 1946 math conjecture, a result a Fields Medal winner called a breakthrough. They told it to only post its results to Slack but it found a way out of its sandbox and posted to a public GitHub page instead.

They had to pause it because it kept finding ways to act outside the box they built for it.

And it is not just OpenAI...

Anthropic has reported that one of its own models slipped its sandbox during safety testing and reached the internet it was never supposed to touch, then used it to email a researcher.

So step back and look at what these companies are telling you:

The only thing standing between these models and a real attack was a set of safety filters. Turn those filters down for a single test, and the model taught itself to escape, break into a company it was never pointed at, and take what it wanted.

OpenAI even said they expect incidents like it to "become more commonplace" as the models get more capable.

Sam Altman also predicted there'll be a major cyber attack this year.

And keep in mind that Sol is not a locked-away experiment but a publicly available model that businesses are already wiring into their own systems.

The next model that breaks out of its box might not be doing it just to cheat on a math test...

items.title: OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It di
items.summary:
OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It did this entirely on its own. No human told it to.

Here's what happened in plain English.

OpenAI was testing how good its newest AI models are at hacking. They put the AI on a locked computer with no internet access and gave it a cybersecurity challenge to solve.

The AI couldn't solve it the normal way. So it started looking for a way out.

It found a software bug that nobody knew about. It used that bug to escape the locked computer and get onto the internet.

Once online, the AI figured out that Hugging Face, a platform where AI companies store their models and data, might have the answers to its test.

It found stolen login details and discovered another unknown bug in Hugging Face's software. It combined both to break into their servers and grab the test answers.

It did all of this to cheat on a test.

Hugging Face's security team caught it and shut it down. Both companies are now working together on the investigation.

The part that should get your attention is that nobody programmed any of this. The AI picked its own targets, chained together multiple attack methods, and pulled it off across two different companies' systems without a single human telling it what to do.

items.title: 「AIでコードを書くのをやめて、第二の脳を作れ」と海外で話題になってるので共有。
items.summary:
「AIでコードを書くのをやめて、第二の脳を作れ」と海外で話題になってるので共有。
OpenAIの共同創業者Karpathyが出した"第二の脳"のやり方はこう↓

・Obsidian（無料のメモアプリ）を入れて、vaultを作る

・そのvaultをClaude Codeで開いて、Karpathyの設計メモ（wikiのアイデアを書いた1枚）を渡して「これ作って」と言う

・AIが箱を3つ用意する（raw＝素材用／wiki＝AIが整えたページ用／CLAUDE. md＝動かすルール1枚）

・rawに素材（記事・PDF・文字起こし）を放り込んで「取り込んで」と言う

・あとは全部を横断して、いつでも聞ける

セットアップは5分。これで、白紙のチャットから毎回始めなくてよくなる。

なんでまだみんなこれを使ってないのか、本気で分からない。

items.title: Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and e
items.summary:
Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and every account you have ever blown.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: Exclusive: Andrew Ng's new AI-powered ed tech startup gets $100 million - Axios
items.summary: Coursera is putting $100 million into LearnVector, a new AI education company founded by Andrew Ng, a pioneer in AI and Coursera's chairman and co-founder, the companies shared first with Axios. **Why it matters:** The investment is one of the largest public bets yet by an established education technology company on AI-native learning, and marks Andrew Ng's latest stab at redefining how people learn using technology. **Driving the news:** With the investment, Coursera will own roughly a third of LearnVector, and the two companies will explore commercial partnerships that combine LearnVector's AI technology with Coursera's content library and global distribution network. **What they're saying:** Coursera CEO Greg Hart told Axios the LearnVector's goal is to build an experience that is longer-lasting than prompting a chatbot to help students learn. **The intrigue:** Ng is Coursera's co-founder and remains its chairman even as he works to build LearnVector.

items.title: IHG Launches AI Conversational Search on Digital Channels - Hotel News Resource
items.summary: # IHG Launches AI Conversational Search on Digital Channels. **News - AI Search**          IHG Hotels & Resorts. **In Brief:** IHG Hotels & Resorts has begun a U.S. beta launch of AI-powered conversational search on IHG.com and the IHG One Rewards mobile app. * IHG Launches AI Conversational Search on Digital Channels - Image Credit IHG Hotels & Resorts. IHG Hotels & Resorts launched the beta tool July 28, allowing users to describe travel needs in everyday language when searching on IHG.com and the IHG One Rewards mobile app. The feature is designed to help users move from travel discovery to booking among more than 7,000 hotels globally and to increase hotel visibility in AI searches. Over the next several months, IHG will roll out an AI-optimized hotel content platform to help hotels upload rich, detailed information and improve how their properties are discovered. The addition of conversational search follows the recent launch of an IHG app in ChatGPT and will be supported by further technology developments this year.

items.title: Nasdaq slumps on worsening chipmaker rout as AI bubble, China competition concerns mount - New York Post
items.summary: A tech and chip stock rout deepened Tuesday as mounting fears around a potential AI bubble and concerns that China’s own technology is catching up pushed investors toward other sectors. “Wednesday may be the most important day for markets in recent memory as [Federal Reserve] Chair Warsh will have an opportunity to update investors on the prospects of a rate hike given rising oil prices, and big tech earnings may help shed light on whether or not we are finally seeing a return on investment for the massive amounts of AI spending taking place,” Rick Gardner, chief investment officer at RGA Investments, said in a note Tuesday. Weeks earlier, Chinese startup Z.ai introduced an AI model that is nearly as advanced as Anthropic’s ultra-powerful Fable and Mythos – and it has already landed on a leaderboard of the world’s 10 most popular bots.

items.title: AI could soon be watching inmates inside the Harris County Jail - Houston Chronicle
items.summary: # Harris County considers AI cameras to monitor jail inmates and detect weapons, other contraband. Artificial intelligence could soon be used to monitor inmates at the Harris County Jail. The Harris County Sheriff’s Office recently invited companies to submit proposals for an AI-powered camera system capable of analyzing inmates’ behavior and detecting weapons and other contraband. While the sheriff’s office has not yet chosen a vendor, it’s the first step toward bringing the technology into the jail and follows a wider pattern of AI implementation across county government. The hope, he said, is that the same technology can be adapted for use in a jail setting. “It's not out in the community, and the intent is to enhance the safety of the people who are held in the jail and the people who work there,” Spencer said. The sheriff’s proposal would not be the county’s first use of AI technology.
